introduction: In the 1980s, India launched a historic program to become self-sufficient in missile manufacturing, which ultimately placed the Indian military among the most powerful in the world.

core_concepts.title: IGMDP (Integrated Guided Missile Development Programme)
core_concepts.description: Started in 1983 under the leadership of Dr. Kalam and successfully completed in 2008. Under this program, 5 major missiles were developed, easily remembered by the acronym **'PATNA'**.

core_concepts.title: The P.A.T.N.A Missiles
core_concepts.description:
1. **Prithvi:** Short-range Surface-to-Surface ballistic missile. 
2. **Agni:** Long-range Surface-to-Surface ballistic missile. 
3. **Trishul:** Short-range Surface-to-Air missile. 
4. **Nag:** 3rd Generation Anti-Tank Guided Missile (ATGM). 
5. **Akash:** Medium-range Surface-to-Air missile.

core_concepts.title: The Power of Agni-V
core_concepts.description: This is the deadliest missile in the Agni series. It is an **ICBM (Intercontinental Ballistic Missile)**. Its strike range is **over 5,000 km**, meaning it can reach all of Asia and parts of Europe, acting as India's ultimate nuclear deterrent.

important_entities.name: Nag Missile
important_entities.significance: Nag is an anti-tank missile designed to destroy heavily armored enemy tanks. It operates on a 'Fire and Forget' principle, meaning once it locks onto a target and is fired, it uses its own infrared seeker to track and hit the moving tank without further guidance. Its helicopter-launched version is called **'Helina'**.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Exam Trap: Questions frequently test the trajectory/domain of these missiles. Prithvi and Agni are Surface-to-Surface. Trishul and Akash are Surface-to-Air. (Trick: You throw a 'Trishul' (Trident) into the air, and 'Akash' literally means sky).

exam_strategy_tips: A favorite question in NDA/CDS: 'Which among the following is a Fire-and-Forget Anti-Tank Guided Missile?' Answer: Nag.
